transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-04 15:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood), Alicia (LumenWare Head of Search), Samir (ML Infra), Rita (Security), Tom (SRE)

[00:00] Evan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick housekeeping, recording on, we'll share notes after. i'm evan from redwood, AE. priya's our se, marco and jasmine on the call as well. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Alicia: good, thanks. excited to go through this — we've been evaluating options for our search stack and want to understand how you handle embeddings + rerank at scale, esp hybrid strategies.
[00:20] Evan: perfect. so agenda: high-level requirements, current infra, throughput and latency targets, routing/top-k tradeoffs, hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and security questions. then next steps. sound ok?
[00:30] Alicia: yep. Samir will kick off with the current stack.
[00:34] Samir: yeah thanks. quick context: lumenware powers product search for enterprise retail customers. about 200M docs across product catalogs, typical query mix is 60% short queries, 30% browsy long queries, 10% complex multi-filter. We currently run an ANN index in-house (milvus for some customers, elastic knn for others) and a lightweight transformer-based reranker. Peak QPS today is around 600 queries/sec across our EU + US regions, with tail latency SLO of 200ms for first-pass recall and 400ms for full rerank.
[01:05] Priya: ok so two-stage pipeline: embed+ANN fanout -> top_k -> rerank. are you doing synchronous rerank for every query?
[01:12] Samir: it depends. for premium customers we do synchronous rerank of top 50, otherwise top 10. but that top50 rerank is killing cost and causing CPU jitter. we were hoping redwood could help lower per-token cost or offload heavy parts.
[01:25] Marco: understood. a few clarifying Qs: what's your average doc embedding dimension and model family? and do you need the embedding generation colocated with ANN ops?
[01:33] Tom: most of our embeddings are 1536 dims using open models, sometimes we test 1024 distilled variants. currently embeddings are generated in our infra and stored; we push them into the ANN service. for secret telemetry reasons we don't want to re-ingest embeddings into an external vendor unless we can use VPC peering or private deployment.
[01:50] Rita: from security: our primary asks are SOC2, SSO/SAML, tenant-level RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration for key management. data residency in EU for EU customers. we need to see logging and retention controls.
[02:05] Priya: yes those are all supported in our dedicated and private options. hosted api can be used too but we'd recommend dedicated or private for your multi-region residency + SSO needs. we'll share the security pack.
[02:16] Alicia: on the routing question — we're worried about hybrid top-k. Samir, can you describe current fanout sizing?
[02:22] Samir: right now for top10 it's 2 shards fanout (approx 20 candidates each), for top50 it hits 6 shards, lots of cross-shard randomness. the issue is tail latency on the rerank, plus cost from token generation when we rerank with an LLM.
[02:38] Priya: two things we typically recommend: (1) smart hybrid routing where small queries use small topk + cached prefixes, and larger exploratory queries go to a higher-throughput pool, and (2) multi-model routing — for example, a distilled 1024-d embedder for first-pass and a higher-quality 1536-d model for rerank or for A/B of premium customers.
[02:55] Alicia: do you have examples of the latency/cost delta for those patterns?
[03:00] Marco: yes, from internal benchmarks: switching from synchronous top50 rerank on our high-quality model to a hybrid approach (top10 with distilled embed+cached rerank for premium asynchronous rerank) reduces cost by ~45% and median latency by ~30%, though tail behavior depends on KV cache hit rates. these numbers vary by query distribution.
[03:20] Samir: interesting. our big worry is maintaining recall — we can't lose high-recall results for power users. how do you validate quality when you reduce dims or use distilled models?
[03:30] Priya: that's where eval prompt sets and canary rollouts come in. Redwood Optimize gives model comparison metrics—embedding similarity recall curves, NDCG on labeled queries. we also recommend a small A/B pilot where you score customer-labeled relevance metrics before rolling wide.
[03:45] Rita: can you explain how KV cache and prefix caching would work with our sharded ANN? we often have hot prefix queries for brand names and categories.
[03:55] Marco: KV cache is per-request token prefix for generation; for retrieval, prefix caching can be done at the ANN result level — we cache top-k results for high-cardinality prefixes. in Redwood Dedicated we can place cache in front of the ANN so rerank doesn't trigger on cached prefixes. with private deployment you can colocate the cache and ANN to avoid network hops.
[04:18] Tom: that sounds promising. any constraints on embedding dimensions for batching throughput? our infra sees bigger dims reduce batch efficiency.
[04:26] Priya: yep higher dims increases per-token memory and reduces effective batch size. In the runtime we have quantized kernels and packed batching strategies that help; still going from 1024->1536 dims is ~1.5x memory and affects throughput. that's why we often recommend mixed-dimension strategies to balance quality and cost.
[04:44] Alicia: on hosting: what's the recommended approach for us — hosted, dedicated, or private? we need EU residency, SSO, predictable latency at peak sales seasons.
[04:53] Evan: based on what you've said I'd recommend a Dedicated cluster per region with VPC peering into your VPC for embedding ingestion + optional private deployment for sensitive customers. Dedicated gives predictable throughput/SLA and is easier to start than full private. we can also provide a hybrid: hosted API for low-sensitivity traffic, dedicated for premium workloads.
[05:10] Samir: cost-wise, how do dedicated commitments compare to hosted per-token? we don't yet know how many tokens/reranks we'll do per month — rough estimate 1-3B tokens if we expand rerank.
[05:20] Marco: committed dedicated capacity is usually more cost-effective per-token at scale because you buy GPU pools. hosted is flexible but gets expensive at heavy rerank volumes. we'll send a modeled comparison in the benchmark template we promised.
[05:32] Alicia: have you seen customers with similar multi-shard ANN setups? any gotchas?
[05:36] Priya: yes, common issues: cross-shard fanout causing tail latency, inconsistent vector normalization across shards, and rebalancing causing temporary recall drops. mitigations: normalized embeddings at generation time, deterministic sharding keys for hotspot control, and read replicas during resharding.
[05:53] Samir: what about fallbacks — if dedicated cluster is saturated, can you route to a cheaper hosted variant with lower quality model?
[05:59] Evan: yes smart routing policies support fallback to compatible model variants, lower-tier infra, or region failover. you'll want to set quality budgets per customer class so premium users rarely see fallback.
[06:12] Rita: security follow-ups: do you support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) and HSM for private deployments?
[06:18] Marco: yes, for Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and support BYOK. Dedicated also supports KMS integrations with customer-managed keys in many cases. we'll include the integration notes in the security pack.
[06:30] Tom: operationally, how do you handle KV cache eviction and consistency across pods? we see cache thrashing during traffic spikes.
[06:38] Priya: we use a mesh-aware cache with soft TTLs and a small write-through for known hot prefixes. you can set cache TTLs per-route. with dedicated or private you can tune those aggressively.
[06:50] Alicia: ok, let's talk about our pilot scope — we want to test hybrid topk routing with a small sample: 2M docs, EU region, peak 800 QPS, rerank top10 for standard, top40 for premium. timeline ideally 3 weeks pilot. thoughts?
[07:07] Priya: feasible. pilot plan: week 1 get data + sample queries, week 2 run bench and small traffic run, week 3 evaluate quality metrics and adjust routing. we'll need the anonymized query histogram and a sample of labeled queries for eval.
[07:20] Samir: we can provide that. any caveats about ingesting embeddings into redwood hosted? we prefer not to send raw embeddings offsite.
[07:28] Marco: you can either generate embeddings on your side and ingest into our Dedicated/Private, or if you prefer hosted we can recommend encryption-in-transit + VPC peering and retention controls; but for regulated data, private is safest.
[07:42] Alicia: pricing ask: can you do a rough ballpark for a dedicated 2-region setup with commit that covers 1-3B tokens and 2 high-throughput GPU pools?
[07:51] Evan: yes we'll send a ballpark in the benchmark/pricing doc. it'll include committed monthly cost and modeled cost-per-rerank for top10/top50 patterns.
[07:59] Rita: also please include compliance packaging and SOC2 docs.
[08:02] Evan: will do.
[08:05] Alicia: any concerns about vector DB compatibility? we use milvus and custom sharding logic, will redwood integrate?
[08:12] Priya: Redwood supports external ANN connectors and can call through to your Milvus endpoints in private/dedicated setups; for hosted we typically ingest vectors into our store but we can federate queries if needed. integration work is typically a 1-2 sprint engineering effort depending on sharding.
[08:28] Samir: ok good.
[08:30] Marco: one more thing—monitoring and cost visibility: Redwood Console will give token-level cost, per-route latency, and per-model cost so you can see rerank cost hotspots and tune routing policies.
[08:44] Alicia: that dashboard visibility is critical for our finance folks.
[08:48] Evan: great. quick recap and next steps?
[08:51] Alicia: yes please.
[08:52] Evan: recap: Redwood recommends dedicated per-region with optional private for high-sensitivity. pilot scope 2M docs, EU region, peak 800 QPS. action items: redwood to send benchmark template, security pack, pricing ballpark; lumenware to share query histograms and sample labels. schedule follow-up SE bench for week of 2026-10-12.
[09:14] Samir: all good from us.
[09:16] Rita: thanks, please send SOC2 artefacts and KMS docs.
[09:19] Evan: will do. thanks everyone.
[09:22] Alicia: thanks all.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., KV cache references transcribed as "K V cache"), some speakers abbreviated, and punctuation approximated.
